My family has farmed this land for generations. I have about 10 mu, most of it flat, decent soil on the North China Plain. My father grew wheat and corn, his father too. I know what works here.

This time of year I am getting the fields ready for winter wheat seeding in October. After wheat comes off in June, I put summer maize straight back in. That rotation is what everyone around here does — two crops a year, same fields. The county extension station pushed some new varieties a few years back and I switched to improved wheat and hybrid maize. Yields went up, so I kept it.

I keep 9 mu in the wheat-maize rotation. I leave 1 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, beans, some cabbage — mostly for the family and a bit to sell at market.

For fertilizer I apply what my neighbor uses and what the agrochemical shop recommends. Probably more nitrogen than I need, but I don't want to risk a poor harvest. Water is getting harder — the well is deeper every year — but I still irrigate wheat three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at grain fill. Maize I irrigate twice if it doesn't rain enough.

I rotary-till before wheat planting. For maize I just plant straight into the wheat stubble — less work and the soil holds moisture better.
